subject: Acuity Health trial — checkpoint action grid and escalation routing
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@acuityhealth.com>, Ethan Price <e.price@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed checkpoint grid (next steps)

Hi Samira / Ethan — thanks for a productive kickoff today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture.

Call highlights:
- Goal: 2-week evaluation to validate Redwood inference for in-app summarization and clinical note generation; focus on throughput and hallucination rate on de-identified sample data.
- Primary success criteria: p95 token latency < 300ms (for 512 tokens), hallucination rate <= 6% on the provided eval set, and < 5% failed responses in streaming mode.
- Resources: Acuity will provide 5k de-identified items and a small labeled holdout set for accuracy checks. Redwood will provision a dedicated trial cluster and a shared debug workspace.

Proposed checkpoint action grid (owners & deadlines):
1) Data handoff and schema validation — owner: Samira (Acuity) /Connor (Redwood) — due: 2027-09-01. Attachment: acuity-eval-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet).
2) Baseline run & smoke tests (sanity/perf) — owner: Marissa (Redwood SE) — due: 2027-09-03. Deliverable: perf log + token cost estimate.
3) Qualitative eval (hallucination spot checks) — owner: Samira/Ethan — due: 2027-09-06.
4) Final acceptance run & sign-off — owner: Michael (Acuity procurement) /Vivek — target: 2027-09-10.

Known risks called out during the call: limited labeled data (Samira), procurement timeline for dedicated cluster approval (Michael), and potential PII redaction gaps during streaming (Ethan). See mitigation ideas below.

Immediate asks: 
- Samira: share the sanitized sample set and schema by end of day 2027-09-01 (reply with Drive link).
- Marissa: paste the smoke test command and expected outputs into the shared Drive doc by 2027-09-02.
- Connor: prepare a short rollback/escalation play (who to call at 3pm PST) in case of blocking infra issues.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-minute checkpoint on 2027-09-03. Thanks — Vivek

--

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed checkpoint grid (next steps)

Thanks Vivek — this looks good. Quick notes:
- We'll export the 5k de-identified records by tomorrow; the clinical ops team needs to run a final scrub — ETA midday 2027-09-01. I'll drop the Drive link in this thread when ready.
- Procurement: Michael flagged an internal review that could shift the sign-off by a few days if the security questionnaire requires additional evidence. We'll try to keep the dedicated cluster option but may accept a hosted trial fallback to keep momentum.

One question on success criteria: is there a preferred metric for "hallucination rate"? We typically use entity-level hallucination on NER spans; would Redwood prefer whole-response factuality or per-entity?

Also CC'ing Michael — Michael, are there any procurement blockers you foresee this week?

Best,
Samira

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@acuityhealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-31T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed checkpoint grid (next steps) — smoke test plan + acceptance checklist

Folks — adding the smoke/perf test details and baseline acceptance checks so the eval is reproducible. I'm attaching a minimal checklist and sample command snippets to the shared Drive (shared/acuity-mtp-roadmap.md).

Smoke test (run on Redwood dedicated trial cluster):
- Command: ./run_eval.sh --input sample-5k.json --model rwd-clarity-7B-q4 --streaming true --max-tokens 512
- Expected perf: p95 latency for 512 tokens < 300ms; median token cost < $0.0009/token (estimate).
- Logs: perf.log, stderr capture, kv-cache stats. Drop artifacts in the Drive folder after run.

Acceptance checklist (baseline):
- All responses returned without 500/timeout errors for the full 5k sample.
- Hallucination metric: primary metric = entity-level mismatch rate on labeled holdout (<= 6%). Secondary = whole-response factuality score (>= 88%).
- Streaming behavior: no more than 5% incomplete streams under targeted concurrency (10 concurrent clients).

If we hit a blocker during the baseline, Connor will triage infra vs model and escalate to the on-call infra engineer (see escalation routing below).

I've also called out mitigation options: fallback to smaller batch sizes, enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, and temporarily pin to an earlier quantized model if inference errors spike.

I'll run the baseline on 2027-09-03 morning and share the perf.log in the Drive.

Thanks — Marissa

--

Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@acuityhealth.com>, Michael Torres <m.torres@acuityhealth.com>, Ethan Price <e.price@acuityhealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-02T17:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed checkpoint grid (next steps) — blocker detected & mitigation plan

Quick ops update after today's smoke run (logs attached in Drive). Summary: baseline run initiated at 15:00 PDT — we observed a repeatable failure pattern when processing batch sizes > 16: the inference process returns a streaming incomplete payload ~0.6% of the time and a separate class of tokenization mismatch errors for longer clinical notes (~1.8% of items).

Immediate mitigations we've applied (temporary):
- Reduced batch size to 8 for the remainder of the run (restored stream completion rate to <0.5%).
- Enabled prefix caching for frequent prompt templates — reduced p95 by ~20ms.
- Switched to the rwd-clarity-7B-q4-v2 (slightly older quant) for the long-note subset which removed the tokenization mismatch errors in our repro.

Open risk items and escalation path:
- Root cause: suspected model-tokenizer mismatch on some multi-byte clinical artifacts. Next step: model engineering needs to validate tokenizer updates and push a patched quant. Owner: Marissa (eng triage) /Model Eng. Target ETA: 2027-09-06.
- Procurement constraint: if dedicated cluster approval is delayed past 2027-09-08, risk to end-date increases; fallback: use hosted trial capacity with data isolation controls. Owner: Michael /Vivek.
- If we see >1% of failed responses after fixes, we escalate to on-call infra and Redwood SRE lead (pager duty) — escalation contact: +1 (415) 555-0202 (SRE on-call) and sres@redwood.com.

Proposed next immediate actions:
1) Marissa to open a model engineering ticket with repro artifacts and tag priority P1.
2) Samira to confirm whether the long notes can be preprocessed to normalize multi-byte markers (short term).
3) Vivek / Michael to confirm procurement fallback decision by 2027-09-04.

I'll monitor the run tomorrow morning and update the thread. If anything is blocking sign-off, we'll do a 15-minute triage call — please mark availability.

Connor

Technical Program Manager | Redwood Inference
